title: Jude and the Letter
premise: In the winter of a collapsing republic, Beatrix Thornbury carries diplomatic dispatches through a provincial town that has never mattered to anyone in power — until a requisitioning army seizes the customs house, the ledgers, and every name inside them. Among the papers is a letter that could either save the town's families or condemn the courier who carries it, forcing Beatrix to choose between the loyalty that raised them and the truth that could free them. Guided by Jude, a local clerk who knows the back roads and the back rooms, they smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints as the front line collapses toward them. The book ends with the letter delivered and the republic gone: Beatrix survives by surrendering their own name to history, while Jude keeps the town's names alive in memory rather than paper.
about_author: Dominic Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of failed states before turning to fiction. They write about the people history forgets to name, and live quietly somewhere with unreliable winters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Paper
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the provincial town of Aldenmoor, Beatrix files dispatches at the customs house, convinced history happens elsewhere. A routine ledger entry — a neighbor's name — unsettles them. Emotional beat: complacency cracked by the first hint that paper can be dangerous.

chapters.title: Jude Counts the Doors
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The town clerk inventories Aldenmoor's households for the census, knowing every family by its debts and secrets. Jude notices Beatrix's careful handwriting and suspects the courier carries more than tariffs. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into quiet watchfulness.

chapters.title: Dispatches from a Dying Republic
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A sealed diplomatic pouch arrives with orders to hold it until a relief convoy comes. Beatrix glimpses one word — names — through a torn corner. Emotional beat: the thrill of importance curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Sound of the Front
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Distant artillery becomes audible; refugees trickle through with contradictory news. Jude's brother urges flight; Jude refuses to abandon the ledgers that prove who owns what. Emotional beat: stubborn rootedness against panic.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Soldiers occupy the customs house at dawn and seize the ledgers — every name in Aldenmoor. An officer named Colonel Vess is polite, thorough, and terrifying. Emotional beat: the horror of watching one's ordinary work become an instrument.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude realizes the seized records include the conscription lists and the letter of safe conduct hidden in the diplomatic pouch — proof that could spare or doom the town. Emotional beat: cold clarity of stakes.

chapters.title: An Offer of Coffee
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Colonel Vess invites Beatrix to tea, probing what the courier knows and offering protection in exchange for cooperation. Beatrix lies for the first time in their life. Emotional beat: the vertigo of deception.

chapters.title: The Back Room Agreement
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude approaches Beatrix with a plan: copy the names, move the letter, use the smugglers' paths Jude's family has used for generations. Beatrix refuses — then doesn't. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix maps the town's three crossings: the bridge, the mill gate, the marsh ford. Each is guarded; each demands a different lie. Emotional beat: the planner's grim arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Daughter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback to Jude's mother's runs through the marsh, and the family debt that made Jude a clerk instead of a smuggler. Emotional beat: inherited courage and inherited shame.

chapters.title: Names on a List
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix reads the seized ledger and finds their own landlord, their baker, the boy who sweeps the office — all listed for transport. Emotional beat: history stops being elsewhere.

chapters.title: The First Copy
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. By lamplight, Jude and Beatrix copy the conscription names into a false hymnal. A knock at the door nearly ends everything. Emotional beat: terror braided with purpose.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The colonel announces the town will be evacuated once the relief convoy is intercepted; the ledgers will travel with him. Beatrix realizes the deadline: three days. Emotional beat: time becoming the enemy.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. First test: Jude crosses the bridge with the hymnal hidden in a coffin of a genuinely dead neighbor, trading on grief as cover. Emotional beat: mourning weaponized, and the guilt of it.

chapters.title: A Betrayal Overheard
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix overhears a clerk in Vess's office selling information — and realizes someone in town has already talked. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root in the alliance.

chapters.title: The Mill Gate Lie
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Second crossing: Jude forges a grain requisition and walks the copies out through the mill, helped by a guard who owes Jude's family. Emotional beat: the fragile currency of old favors.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Carries
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Interlude: Beatrix's backstory as an orphan of the last war, raised by the diplomatic service to be loyal to paper, not people. Emotional beat: identity as something assigned, not chosen.

chapters.title: The Letter Itself
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude finally reads the diplomatic letter: it is a promise of amnesty, signed and sealed, never delivered — proof the republic abandoned them knowingly. Emotional beat: rage at the truth.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix confronts the choice: deliver the letter as duty demands, or use it to save the town. Vess tightens surveillance. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Informant's Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude identifies the informant — the brother who urged flight. Confrontation in the smokehouse; no resolution, only wounds. Emotional beat: family as the first casualty of truth.

chapters.title: Curfew
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The army locks the town; the mill gate route dies. Only the marsh ford remains. Beatrix and Jude argue about whether the letter is worth a life. Emotional beat: love and pragmatism at odds.

chapters.title: The Hymnal Returns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The copied names reach the partisan camp across the marsh — but the partisans want the original letter too, and their price is steep. Emotional beat: allies with their own ledgers.

chapters.title: Vess Suspects
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The colonel summons Beatrix, lays out discrepancies, and gives one night to confess. Beatrix holds the lie by a thread. Emotional beat: the loneliest hour.

chapters.title: A Night of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude bribes, forges, and begs across half the town in a single night to prepare the ford crossing. Emotional beat: the town quietly choosing sides.

chapters.title: The Convoy Burns
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The relief convoy is ambushed on the road; the republic's last authority in the region dissolves. Vess declares martial law and orders the ledgers loaded at dawn. Emotional beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: The Marsh Ford
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Third crossing: Beatrix and Jude wade the ford at night with the letter and the true ledger, ice in the reeds, a sentry's lantern sweeping. Emotional beat: the body's fear against the will's resolve.

chapters.title: Caught at the Far Bank
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A patrol takes them — but the partisans take the patrol. In the chaos the letter is nearly lost in the water; Jude saves it at the cost of the ledger. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured in paper.

chapters.title: Which Truth to Tell
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The partisans demand the letter for their own bargaining. Beatrix must decide whose hands history flows through. Emotional beat: the ethics of evidence.

chapters.title: Vess's Last Audit
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Vess, facing his own superiors' failure, burns what ledgers remain and prepares to flee — but keeps one copy, the one with Beatrix's name in the margins. Emotional beat: the hunter becoming a debtor.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude trades the letter's delivery route to the partisans in exchange for the town's names being struck from transport lists — a bargain made with Beatrix's silence. Emotional beat: loyalty renegotiated.

chapters.title: The Letter Moves
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The letter travels by partisan hand toward the neutral border, Beatrix's testimony attached. Beatrix feels lighter and more hollow than ever. Emotional beat: letting go of the thing that defined them.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With the ledgers burned, the townspeople begin reciting names from memory at the well each evening — an oral ledger. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into ritual.

chapters.title: Vess Comes for Beatrix
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The colonel, fleeing, offers Beatrix escape and erasure in exchange for the letter's route. Beatrix refuses and lets him ride into the collapsing front. Emotional beat: the quiet triumph of refusal.

chapters.title: The Front Arrives
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The new army rolls in — different flags, same requisitions. Jude hides the hymnal in the church wall. Emotional beat: history repeating as farce and threat.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the border archive, Beatrix gives sworn testimony, surrendering their courier's name and number to become simply a witness. Emotional beat: identity dissolved into truth.

chapters.title: The Amnesty Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Weeks later, the letter's contents reach Aldenmoor; the transport lists are voided. The town reads the republic's broken promise aloud and chooses to honor it anyway. Emotional beat: bitter, hard-won grace.

chapters.title: What Jude Kept
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude opens the church wall and finds the hymnal safe, then adds one name of their own to its pages. Emotional beat: authorship of memory.

chapters.title: Beatrix Returns
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix comes back to Aldenmoor with no commission, no seal, no letter — only themselves. Jude meets them at the bridge, the first checkpoint, now unguarded. Emotional beat: arrival without papers.

chapters.title: The Second Copy
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Beatrix and Jude copy the hymnal together, one reading names, one writing, deciding who else should ever see them. Emotional beat: partnership as the answer to loyalty's question.

chapters.title: The Letter and the Names
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring: the letter is framed in the customs house, the hymnal hidden behind it. Beatrix files nothing; Jude records everything. Emotional beat: belonging found not in history's archives but in each other's keeping.
